title: BFL Friction Fix (τ=ν·u_t/q) Verification: SUBOFF + Cylinder
fix_description: When BFL is active, friction drag uses τ=ν·u_t/q instead of standard τ=2ν·u_t (=ν·u_t/0.5). q_wall is the average BFL q-value per near-wall cell. When q=0.5, the fix reduces to the standard formula.

analysis.fix_effect_on_friction: BFL no fix Cd_f=0.1028 → BFL+fix Cd_f=0.0740 (28% reduction). Expected from formula: 0.5/0.7321=0.683, so 0.1028*0.683=0.0702. Actual 0.0740 is close (flow field still converging).
analysis.fix_vs_standard_bb: BFL+fix Cd_f=0.074 is still 1.9x higher than standard BB Cd_f=0.039. The BFL flow field has different near-wall velocities than standard BB.
analysis.pressure_drag: Cd_p nearly identical: BFL+fix=0.00526 vs standard BB=0.00539. BFL correctly handles pressure.
analysis.total_error: BFL no fix: 157.4% → BFL+fix: 88.8% → standard BB: 5.6%. Fix improves BFL but doesn't match standard BB.
analysis.expected_vs_actual: Expected ~5-6% after fix (similar to standard BB). Actual: 88.8%. The fix alone is insufficient because the BFL flow field itself produces different near-wall velocities.

analysis.q_value_impact: Cylinder q_mean=0.392 < 0.5, so the fix INCREASES friction (1/q > 2). This is opposite to SUBOFF where q_mean=0.735 > 0.5.
analysis.fix_effect_on_friction: BFL+fix Cd_f=0.829 vs standard BB Cd_f=0.184 (4.5x higher). The fix correctly accounts for closer wall distance but the BFL near-wall velocities are much higher.
analysis.pressure_drag: BFL+fix Cd_p=1.309 vs standard BB Cd_p=1.449. BFL pressure drag is actually closer to ref Cd=1.30.
analysis.total_error: BFL+fix: 64.5% vs standard BB: 25.6%. The fix makes BFL worse for the cylinder because q<0.5 increases friction.
analysis.physics: For q<0.5, the wall is closer to the near-wall fluid cell. The fix τ=ν·u_t/q correctly increases friction to account for the steeper gradient. However, the BFL flow field produces much higher near-wall velocities than standard BB, compounding the effect.

key_findings: The BFL friction fix (τ=ν·u_t/q) is mathematically correct: it reduces to τ=2ν·u_t when q=0.5 (standard half-way BB).
SUBOFF (q_mean=0.735 > 0.5): Fix reduces friction by 28% (0.103→0.074), improving total error from 157% to 89%. But still 1.9x higher friction than standard BB (0.039).
Cylinder (q_mean=0.392 < 0.5): Fix INCREASES friction (1/q > 2), making BFL+fix worse (64.5% vs 25.6% error for standard BB).
The fix alone is insufficient to match standard BB because the BFL flow field produces different near-wall velocities than standard BB staircase walls.
Pressure drag is well-handled by BFL in both cases (similar to or better than standard BB).
The q-value distribution matters: q>0.5 (wall farther) → fix helps; q<0.5 (wall closer) → fix hurts relative to standard BB.
For a linear velocity profile, τ=ν·u_t/q gives the exact shear stress regardless of q. The discrepancy arises because near-wall cells are not in the viscous sublayer at these grid resolutions.
